findings.title: Integer 0 expands as empty value in ? / & / ; expansions
findings.property: a scalar int n expands to its decimal string in query and path-parameter expansion
findings.actual: '?x=' and ';x' (0 is treated as empty string by a truthiness check `if value:`)
findings.evidence: ScalarVariableValue includes int; RFC 6570 only treats the empty string as empty (3.2.7/3.2.8), 0 is defined and stringifies to '0'; other ints like 1 expand correctly.

review.title: Integer 0 expands as empty value in ? / & / ; expansions

findings.reproSource:
from uritemplate.variable import URIVariable


def test_repro_zero():
    assert URIVariable("?x").expand({"x": 0})["?x"] == "?x=0"
    assert URIVariable(";x").expand({"x": 0})[";x"] == ";x=0"

findings.title: Reserved/fragment expansion skips encoding when value contains any percent-escape
findings.property: output of {+var} contains no characters outside reserved/unreserved/pct-encoded
findings.actual: 'a b%41' (value returned unchanged because unquote(value) != value)
findings.evidence: RFC 6570 3.2.3: reserved expansion passes through only pct-encoded triplets and reserved/unreserved characters; every other character (e.g. space) must be percent-encoded.

review.title: Reserved/fragment expansion leaves unsafe characters unencoded when the value contains any percent-escape
review.reason: RFC 6570 §3.2.3 lets `{+var}` and `{#var}` pass through only reserved characters, unreserved characters and existing pct-encoded triplets. `_only_quote_unquoted_characters` is all-or-nothing: if `unquote(value) != value` it returns the whole value untouched. So `'a b%41'` comes out with a raw space, which is not a valid URI, while `'a b'` correctly becomes `'a%20b'`. The heuristic is deliberate, and the spec fixtures only cover values with no escapes or with a bare `%`. It is still a real spec deviation, and a regex-based fix that quotes everything except valid `%XX` triplets is simple, though a maintainer might treat it as a low-priority edge case.

review.title: Integer 0 expands as empty in {?x} and {;x}

findings.reproSource:
from uritemplate.api import expand


def test_repro_zero_query():
    assert expand("{?a}", {"a": 0}) == "?a=0"
    assert expand("{;a}", {"a": 0}) == ";a=0"

findings.title: partial() leaves variable unexpanded when value is empty string
findings.property: partial with all variables supplied equals expand
findings.evidence: partial docs: only missing params stay in the template; x was given. template._expand uses `expanded.get(...) or var`, conflating empty expansion with absent.

propertyCheck.example:
Failing test case: test_partial_full_equals_expand(

    v='',
)

review.title: partial() keeps {var} in the template when the supplied value expands to an empty string
review.reason: URITemplate._expand uses `expanded.get(match_group) or var` in replace_partial. That treats an empty expansion, which is what a supplied '' produces for `{x}`, the same as a variable that was never supplied. So `partial('a{x}b', {'x': ''})` returns `a{x}b` while `expand` returns `ab`. The docstring says only missing parameters should remain, and the fix is small: test whether the key is absent or the variable was supplied, instead of testing truthiness. The case is an edge one, but a maintainer would probably accept the fix.

findings.evidence: VariableValue type allows int; RFC 6570 prefix applies to the string form; value[:prefix] is applied without str() conversion in variable.py.

review.title: Prefix modifier (`{var:N}`) raises TypeError on int/float scalar values
review.reason: `ScalarVariableValue` explicitly includes int, float and complex, and `Operator.quote` already converts non-strings with `str()` (variable.py:159). So `{a}` with `a=12` works, but `{a:1}` slices the raw int at variable.py:450 (the same pattern appears at lines 315, 368 and 417) and raises `TypeError: 'int' object is not subscriptable`. RFC 6570 applies the prefix to the string form, so the expected result `'1'` is correct. The existing tests only use string values, so nothing documents the crash as intended, and a maintainer would likely accept a small `str(value)[:prefix]` fix.
